s1.quote: Sunset House Reef is accessible from the shore … The legendary Sunset House Reef is a haven for macro photography enthusiasts and offers incredible experiences at all times of day, including night dives

s2.quote: Sunset (House) Reef / Siren of Amphitrite A popular shore dive, the reef has plenty of coral, sponges and sea whips to see while the 9 foot tall bronze mermaid statue

highlights.text: Submerged bronze mermaid statue (Amphitrite)
Macro life; good for night dives
Coral, sponges and sea whips

summary.text: A shore-entry house reef at Sunset House in George Town, popular for macro photography and night dives. Expect healthy coral, sponge and sea-whip growth, a nine-foot bronze mermaid statue underwater and a small landing-craft wreck nearby.

s1.quote: At its most shallow, the wreck of Kittiwake was 15 feet (4.6 meters) below the water's surface and at its deepest, 64 feet (20 meters) below the surface

s2.quote: Kittiwake Wreck Ranging in depth from 15 to 65 feet (5-20m) deep, this former US Navy submarine rescue vessel … The ship is 251 feet (76m) long and has 5 decks to explore

s3.quote: Ex USS Kittiwake … The wreck has been made extremely diver friendly. So much so that you do not need to have a wreck certification to dive on it

highlights.text: Five decks to explore; ex US Navy rescue ship
Open, diver-friendly layout

access.value: Wreck certification not required; follow an instructor if not wreck-certified

summary.text: A 251 ft former US Navy submarine rescue ship sunk as an artificial reef off Seven Mile Beach in 2011. It lies in roughly 15 to 65 ft of water and was prepared for diving, so it suits recreational divers without wreck training.

s1.quote: Oro Verde Wreck About 50 feet (15m) deep, this 184 foot (56m) long steel cargo vessel was sunk in 1980 and has since broken up

s2.quote: Paradise Reef/Oro Verde Wreck - max depth 50 feet

s3.quote: the nearby Oro Verde wreck too. This former Venezuelan freighter sitting on the seafloor has become an artificial reef where you may spot groupers, barracudas, and eagle rays

highlights.text: 184 ft steel cargo ship, broken up against the reef
Groupers, barracuda, eagle rays, jacks

summary.text: A 184 ft steel freighter sunk in 1980 in about 50 ft of water just off Seven Mile Beach. Now broken up against the reef, it is a shallow wreck with jacks, groupers and eels, often dived together with neighbouring Paradise Reef.

s1.quote: Paradise Reef/Oro Verde Wreck - max depth 50 feet … Arguably one of the best shallow dive sites in Grand Cayman! Paradise reef is fantastic on it’s own

s2.quote: Paradise Reef This relatively shallow site is about 35 feet (11m) deep and features a spur and groove coral reef covered in sponges and with plenty of fish

highlights.text: Spur-and-groove reef covered in sponges
Dived with the nearby Oro Verde wreck

summary.text: A shallow spur-and-groove reef off Seven Mile Beach, covered in sponges and busy with fish. Boats usually pair it with the neighbouring Oro Verde wreck for an easy, shallow dive.

s1.quote: Scuba diving at Turtle Reef, a mini wall with a sharp descent to around 60 feet, is a highlight

highlights.text: Mini-wall dropping to about 60 ft

s1.quote: Devil’s Grotto … huge, hulking coral heads with swim-throughs, caverns, and open chimneys … At its shallowest, Devil’s Grotto is only 14ft (four metres) deep … The maximum depth here is 50 feet (15 meters) and there is easy access from the shore

s2.quote: Eden Rock / Devil’s Grotto Close to George Town and with a maximum depth of 45 feet (14m), these sites are very popular and are ideal for shore dives

highlights.text: Swim-throughs, caverns and chimneys in coral heads
Silverside schools, tarpon and barracuda

summary.text: A shallow shore dive off George Town built around big coral heads riddled with swim-throughs, caverns and chimneys. It tops out within a few feet of the surface, reaches about 45 to 50 ft, and is popular with beginners and snorkellers.

s1.quote: Trinity Caves - max depth 100 feet … a series of 3 large, beautiful swim-throughs that weave in and out of the main reef, bringing you out on the wall at around 80 feet

s2.quote: Trinity Caves This popular dive site, ranging in depth from 50 to 70 feet ( 15-21m) deep, has made the pages of dive magazines due to it’s trinity (three) of grottoes with long swim-throughs

s3.quote: Trinity Caves … labyrinthine passages and swim-throughs winding through the main reef

highlights.text: Three long swim-throughs exiting onto the wall
Moray eels and nudibranchs in side chambers

summary.text: A West Wall favourite where three long swim-throughs wind through the reef and emerge on the wall around 80 ft. The dive tops out near 100 ft and finishes on the wall top, with sponges, gorgonians, crustaceans and moray eels along the way.

s1.quote: Doc Poulson Wreck This former cable laying ship sits in 50 feet (15m) of water and is home to plenty of coral growth as well as young fish

highlights.text: Former cable-laying ship covered in coral
Young fish on the wreck

s1.quote: Aquarium North & South - max depth 50 feet … Aquarium North & South are always a great choice! Follow the coral fingers around at the start of your dive keeping an eye out in the sand for Garden Eels, Stingrays

s2.quote: Aquarium (Reef) This relatively shallow site is about 35 feet (11m) deep and is home to lots of coral and tons of fish including sergeant majors, angelfish and snappers. A great spot for beginners

s3.quote: Aquarium, close to the Kittiwake wreck off Seven Mile Beach, is home to stunning coral formations, a wide range of tropical fish, and majestic sea turtles

highlights.text: Coral fingers, garden eels and stingrays in the sand
Dense fish life; sea turtles

summary.text: A shallow reef next to the Kittiwake off Seven Mile Beach, with coral fingers, sand patches holding garden eels and stingrays, and thick schools of tropical fish. Easy depths make it a good choice for beginners.

s1.quote: Eagle Ray Pass - max depth 100 feet … Eagle Ray Pass is a deep coral chasm leading to the wall … a regular gathering place for Eagle Rays that cruise along the face of the wall

s2.quote: Eagle Ray Pass: A firm favourite amongst regular Cayman divers. A spectacular canyonway cuts through the reef here and spills you onto the wall at 100ft … the top of the wall is only at 45ft

highlights.text: Coral canyon spilling onto the wall
Eagle rays cruising along the wall
Sponges, gorgonians and black coral

summary.text: A North Wall dive where a coral canyon cuts through the reef and spills onto a near-vertical wall at about 100 ft, with the wall top only about 45 ft down. Eagle rays are regular visitors along the wall face.

s1.quote: Eagle Ray Rock Starting around 50 feet (15m) deep, this steep vertical wall has a cut and ravine feature along with colorful sponges, large coral pillars and plenty of rays

highlights.text: Cut and ravine on a steep vertical wall
Colourful sponges, coral pillars, rays

s1.quote: Big Dipper For advanced divers, this wall plunges more than 70 feet (21m) deep
